To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
we have detected solar-like oscillations in a large sample (N=500) of solar type stars observed by the NASA Kepler mission.

the distribution of stellar masses of solar-type stars in the Galaxy is different from that predicted by current stellar evolution theory, and that the distribution of masses of stars in the Kepler sample is consistent with the distribution of stellar ages, which is in turn consistent with the observed distribution of stellar luminosities.

the observed masses of the stars in the Kepler asteroseismology sample differ from those of the synthetic population models in a way that is consistent with the observed mass-radius relation and that these stars are younger than the population models predict.

the study of solar type stars and their properties.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the observed mass distribution of stars in the Kepler mission is significantly different from that predicted by stellar population synthesis models, and that the observed distribution is more similar to the distribution of masses in the solar neighbourhood.

stellar models of solar type stars are not yet accurate enough to be used as reliable tracers of stellar populations.
